SMTO-SKL-0164 — GitHub has paused requests from your account for a while

GUID: 30acf436-cee4-5953-9352-04b2740f3e26
Slug: github-rate-limited
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • Your GitHub account has used all the requests GitHub allows in a set time. GitHub refused this one, so it changed nothing. Requests work again after the reset time.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in the conversation how long GitHub said to wait. The step's result records the number of seconds. GitHub sets a fixed reset time for your account's allowance, and SMTO refuses new GitHub requests from this token until then.
  2. Wait until that time has passed, then repeat your request. Requests made before the reset are refused straight away.
  3. If this happens often, ask SMTO for fewer GitHub lookups at once, such as one page of results instead of many. Each lookup uses part of the same allowance.

What success looks like

  • After the wait, your request completes without a limit message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't switch to a different token just to get around the limit.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GitHub returned 403/429 with rate-limit headers and x-ratelimit-remaining=0, so the primary rate limit is exhausted until reset_at.

What this means

  • HTTP 403/429 has rate-limit evidence and the recorded remaining request count is zero, producing the primary-limit classification. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • HTTP 403/429 has rate-limit evidence and the recorded remaining request count is zero, producing the primary-limit classification.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect remaining, reset_at and Retry-After for the affected resource.

How to fix it

  • GitHubClient.error classifies rate_limited when remaining is 0 and records a per-token backoff until reset_at/Retry-After (held in process memory, so later calls fail fast). Wait until retry_after/reset_at shown in details, then retry; reduce request volume, and do not rotate tokens to bypass the limit.
  • Wait until reset_at and retry_after permit another request. Do not immediately retry or switch tokens to bypass the limit.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Further requests wait until the recorded primary limit permits them.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
